newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields share surge fuels takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields share surge fuels takeover talk.

text.p: A surge in the share price of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd has reignited speculation that the group could be the target of a takeover bid, analysts and dealers said.
The stock has jumped from 124 rand on October 21, hitting a year high of 153.50 on Thursday before easing slightly to close at 150.00 rand.
The group's weak September quarter results had highlighted the vulnerability of the company, long mentioned as a possible takeover target, analysts said.
"I think there is something going on," John Clemmow, mining analyst at Fergusson Bros, said on television on Thursday night.

"We know that Newmont from America has been looking and we hear Gencor, possibly in conjunction with Anglo (American) and maybe even Randgold, are also having a sniff around. But I think it's early (days)."

Gold Fields deputy chairman Alan Wright told Business Day newspaper that the increase in the share price was probably attributable to the group's unhedged policy which meant it would benefit from a higher rand gold price following the fall in the currency.
